releases.name: 0.10.4 — interrupted replies
releases.body:
## Interrupted replies

- `/annotate`, `/annotate-pick` and `/ref` now use the text of an interrupted reply, such as
  one stopped while its questions were waiting for an answer. Previously `/annotate`
  reported that the session had no completed reply, even though the reply was on screen.

Real failures and replies that are still streaming stay excluded. Automatic review still
never opens for an interrupted turn. No options, keys or stored annotations change.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+**, Node **22+**. Native reviewers are included for macOS arm64/x64,
Linux arm64/x64 (glibc 2.35+), and Windows x64.

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
# Existing installation:
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Run `/reload` or reopen OpenCode if the reviewer has not refreshed.

## Verification

Node tests, Rust formatting/Clippy/workspace checks, 21 isolated OpenCode smoke scenarios
and the `/ref` reference smoke passed locally. Release automation builds native reviewers
for all five supported targets and verifies the npm package.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.10.3...v0.10.4)

releases.name: v0.10.3 — long code lines and compose cursor
releases.body:
## Long code lines and compose cursor

- Long lines in code blocks now wrap at the edge of the view instead of being cut off, so
  every character stays readable and can be selected and annotated. Spacing and
  indentation are kept; tables reflow as before.
- The comment box cursor stays inside the box: when a row is exactly full, the cursor moves
  to the start of the next row instead of rendering over the last wide character.

No options, keys or stored annotations change.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+**, Node **22+**. Native reviewers are included for macOS arm64/x64,
Linux arm64/x64 (glibc 2.35+), and Windows x64.

```sh

# Existing installation:

```

Run `/reload` or reopen OpenCode if the reviewer has not refreshed.

## Verification

Node tests, Rust formatting/Clippy/workspace checks (including code-wrap and compose-cursor
regressions), and 21 isolated OpenCode smoke scenarios passed locally. Release automation
builds native reviewers for all five supported targets and verifies the npm package.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.10.2...v0.10.3)

releases.name: v0.10.2 — table cell selection
releases.body:
## Table cells select cleanly

- A mouse drag or `v` selection that starts in a table cell now stays in that cell. Dragging
  down a wrapped cell quotes only that cell instead of pulling in the neighbouring columns.
- Overshooting the cell's last line stops at its edge. Dragging into another column still
  selects whole rows, so a quote across several cells remains possible.

No options, keys or stored annotations change.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+**, Node **22+**. Native reviewers are included for macOS arm64/x64,
Linux arm64/x64 (glibc 2.35+), and Windows x64.

releases.name: 0.10.1 — automatic review and blank-session web pairing
releases.body:
## Start web review from a blank session

- Run `/annotate-web` from OpenCode's blank home screen. Annotate creates and pairs an
  empty session in the current directory with your selected model; no initial prompt is needed.
- URL and local HTML targets work from home too. Sending notes stays bound to the created
  session even after you switch tabs. Invalid targets and `off` do not create a session.

## Automatic review for long replies

- **Opt in to automatic annotation.** Set `autoAnnotate: true` to open the bundled reviewer after a successful reply in the active session exceeds `autoAnnotateThreshold`. Public defaults remain off and 2,000 Unicode characters; a reply exactly at the threshold does not open the reviewer.
- **Review the exact reply once.** Background, failed and interrupted turns are skipped. Duplicate completion events and configuration reloads do not reopen an already handled reply. Sending feedback remains an explicit action.
- **JSONC settings reach the terminal reliably.** A location-scoped configuration RPC carries server-loaded options to the TUI on OpenCode 2.2, including hot reloads. Existing theme and input-source settings continue to apply.

This release includes the bundled TUI and conversation-reference features from
[0.10.0](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/releases/tag/v0.10.0).
Automatic review first ships in **0.10.1**.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+**, Node **22+**. Native reviewers are included for macOS arm64/x64,
Linux arm64/x64 (glibc 2.35+), and Windows x64. Interactive OpenCode handoff is verified on macOS.

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
# Existing installation:
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Configure one plugin entry in `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{
    "package": "@nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest",
    "options": {
      "inheritTheme": true,
      "autoAnnotate": true,
      "autoAnnotateThreshold": 2000
    }
  }]
}
```

Move an older TUI-only entry out of `cli.json`, preserving its options, and remove an old
`binary` override to use the bundled reviewer. Layout settings live in
`~/.config/opencode-annotate/tui.toml`. Run `/reload` if commands have not refreshed.

## Verification

80 Node tests, Rust formatting/Clippy/workspace checks, and 21 isolated OpenCode smoke
scenarios passed locally. The blank-home workflow was also tested and accepted by the maintainer.
Release automation builds native reviewers for all five supported targets and verifies the npm package.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.10.0...v0.10.1)

releases.name: 0.10.0 — integrated TUI and conversation references
releases.body:
## One package for the whole review workflow

- **Annotate TUI is included.** The terminal reviewer, its source and its tests now live in `tui/` in this repository. The npm package ships native executables for macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64 and Windows x64, built from the same release commit. A separate reviewer installation is no longer needed.
- **Your familiar review controls stay available.** Theme inheritance, one-key send, input-method switching, document-width settings and the Chinese bold-label rendering fix are included.
- **Bring another conversation into this one.** `/ref` searches this project's conversations; `/ref --all` searches across projects. Select and confirm a bounded, attributed reference. It is queued without starting an idle assistant.
- **Agents can retrieve history too.** `annotate.session_search` and `annotate.session_read` provide paginated access, including pre-compaction history, with explicit source IDs and text limits.

## Install or update

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0+** and Node **22+**.

```sh
# First installation
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest

# Update an existing installation
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

### Migrating from a TUI-only installation

Keep one plugin entry in `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc`, moving the old entry out of
`cli.json` and preserving its options. This enables both the server tools and terminal
commands. Remove an old `binary` override to select the bundled reviewer.

Layout and key settings now live in `~/.config/opencode-annotate/tui.toml`; copy any
customized layout there once. `inheritTheme: true` continues to use the active OpenCode
palette. Run `/reload` if commands have not refreshed.

Linux binaries require glibc 2.35+ (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer). Windows native builds and
tests are included; interactive OpenCode handoff has been verified on macOS. Full-history
agent reads require the managed OpenCode service; `/ref` uses the connected TUI client.

Original terminal-reviewer MIT copyright notices are retained in `tui/LICENSE`.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/compare/v0.9.1...v0.10.0)
